translation: The Du is the sea of the yang vessels. Its vessel arises below the kidney within the uterus, reaches the lower abdomen, then descends in the waist, at the center of the pubic bone enclosure, connecting to the end of the urinary orifice; in men it runs along the penis down to the u篡u (perineum); in women it connects the genitals and joins at the perineum. Both encircle behind the perineum at the Pingshi point. (Between the front and back genitals.) It separately encircles the buttocks to Shaoyin, and with the middle collateral of Taiyang, joins Shaoyin ascending the inner border of the thigh, and from Huiyang (BL35) (beside the coccyx, two points in all) pierces the spine and meets at the Changqiang point (GV1).
